sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Off-Price Wholesale Liquidation of Branded Overstock Apparel

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (Federal State; Alberta is a common law province)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA)
Canada–United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada–UK TCA)
Canada–United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46 (money laundering offences); Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, s 21.1 (significant control persons register); Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, Part 1 and related regulations; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) reporting and record-keeping rules under PCMLTFA.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign parent company certificate of good standing
Certified true copies of passport pages for officers, directors and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the individual's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Alberta registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the principal's country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list (under the Special Economic Measures Act, United Nations Act, and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act), UN Security Council sanctions, and domestic PEP databases; for US-dollar transactions, OFAC SDN list screening is also recommended. Screening must be completed before incorporation and updated on a risk-based cyclical basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry – Corporate Online system, Government of Alberta; NUANS pre-clearance name search report required
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English or French; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The name must include one of the legal elements 'Limited', 'Limitée', 'Incorporated', 'Incorporée', 'Corporation', or a prescribed abbreviation. Names in a third language are permitted only if the name is otherwise distinctive and does not create confusion with a registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative review request with the Registrar of Corporations (Government of Alberta), setting out the grounds for appeal and supporting evidence, such as consent from the relevant regulatory body or a corrected NUANS report. The Registrar will issue a written decision within 30 business days. If the rejection is upheld, the applicant may submit a new name reservation or apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an off-price wholesale apparel trading company, a virtual office is generally permissible as long as a physical registered office is maintained in Alberta for service of process. However, the Canada Revenue Agency may expect the entity to have real commercial substance, including locally maintained books and records, a Canadian bank account, and a place of effective management; pure mail-forwarding arrangements increase audit exposure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated 5% annual likelihood of a CRA GST/HST books-and-records examination or income tax audit; unannounced corporate registry inspections are rare and generally triggered only by complaints or materially defective filings.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NUANS name search and reservation fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / NUANS service provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Alberta incorporation statutory filing fee (Articles of Incorporation)
UBO register initial preparation and filing (significant control persons registry)
Notarization and apostille of corporate documents (POA, passport copies, certificate of good standing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notaries public and competent authorities in countries of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; varies by issuing jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CRA business number and GST/HST account registration
Corporate records book and minute book setup
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Legal or corporate secretarial service provider

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), ss. 4-22 (incorporation), s. 21 (registered office), s. 23 (share consideration); alternative federal regime: Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss. 8-19
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction — Registry Online (CORES) portal; Corporations Branch
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 — Articles of Incorporation; Certificate of Incorporation issued under s. 9 of the ABCA
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrowed capital fund requirement under the ABCA — common shares may be issued without par value for money, property or past services
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share subscription of the sole founding subscriber is accepted and 1,000 common shares are issued at the directors' fixed subscription price, fully paid before issuance; that the registered office is fixed at the address recorded in the Articles of Incorporation; that the persons named in the Certificate of Incorporation are appointed first directors, and the following officers are appointed: President, Secretary and Treasurer; that the by-laws presented are approved and adopted; and that management is directed to complete all post-incorporation filings, including the Canada Revenue Agency business number, GST/HST registration, municipal business licence and applicable permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Corporate Name Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via an accredited NUANS service provider or Registry Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed corporate names for a NUANS pre-clearance search to verify distinctiveness and availability in Alberta; select a corporate legal element suffix (Inc. or Corp.) as required by the ABCA; obtain the NUANS report which reserves the approved name for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Three proposed corporate names in order of preference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for resemblance or confusion, file a revised NUANS search with a new distinctive name; a 90-day reservation may be renewed once before expiry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and Issuance of Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Registry Online (CORES) electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit Form 1 — Articles of Incorporation electronically, stating the corporate name, the physical registered office address in Alberta, the share structure (e.g., unlimited number of common shares without par value), and the names and consent of the first directors; pay the CAD 100 filing fee and receive the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: First director names, addresses and consent
Registered office physical address in Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Registry Online rejects the articles for deficiency, file corrected articles immediately using CORES; clerical errors may be cured by filing Articles of Correction without retroactive effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organization Meeting, By-laws and Corporate Records Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation; Registered Records Office at the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first directors' meeting or adopt written resolutions to approve the first board resolution, adopt by-laws, issue share certificates, designate the registered records office, and open the corporate minute book, share register and register of directors and officers.
required_dossiers: Written or minuted first board resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defects in the organization meeting may be cured by supplemental board resolution; if any officer appointment is later invalidated, a corrective corporate resolution shall be recorded and the register of directors updated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency Business Number and Program Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with the CRA to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) and open program accounts for corporate income tax, GST/HST, payroll source deductions (if employees are hired) and import/export (if cross-border stock is traded); the GST/HST registration is mandatory once worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000.
required_dossiers: Legal corporate name and directors' particulars
Estimated annual taxable revenue and first GST/HST return period
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA queries the registration particulars, correct the data via My Business Account; the GST/HST effective date may be amended retroactively to the first day of commercial activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Premises Zoning Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary Business Licence Section (or the municipality of the registered office, e.g., City of Edmonton)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence categorizing the activity as wholesale trade of wearing apparel; submit proof of the CRA Business Number, a lease or ownership document for the warehouse/office premises, and a zoning compliance confirmation; pay the annual licence fee before commencing operations.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or title document for premises
Zoning compliance letter or land-use approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the premises are not zoned for wholesale use, file a discretionary development permit application or select premises in an M-CG, I-C or equivalent commercial/industrial district; the licence may then be re-issued with the wholesale classification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Alberta Workers' Compensation Board Registration and Warehousing Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Workers' Compensation Board of Alberta (WCB-Alberta) — Employer Account Services; municipal fire authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the corporation employs warehouse or delivery staff, open a WCB employer account and obtain the applicable industry classification and premium rate; conduct a fire marshal inspection and OHS manifest inspection of the warehouse for fire extinguishers, emergency exits and manual handling protocols for garment bales.
required_dossiers: Estimated annual payroll and job-duty descriptions
Fire safety and OHS inspection certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the WCB assigns a higher industry classification, submit a classification review request with a detailed business activity statement; any OHS order must be remediated and a reinspection requested within the compliance deadline.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No provincial industrial licensing board applies to off-price wholesale apparel liquidation; municipal authority: City of Calgary/Edmonton Business Licence Section; occupational authority: WCB-Alberta and Alberta OHS
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence — Wholesale Trade (Wearing Apparel); no separate Alberta manufacturing/industrial operating permit is required

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no full EIA required; warehouse and wholesale distribution of finished garments is not a Schedule 1 activity under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater discharge or industrial VOC emissions expected; stormwater runoff from the warehouse site must meet municipal drainage bylaws and applicable Alberta ambient air quality objectives; returned or unsold finished garments must be disposed of through approved municipal solid waste streams and, if donated, through licensed charitable collectors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire marshal (annual inspection, fire extinguishers, illuminated exits, and sprinkler compliance for warehouses above 1,500 m²); structural load inspection for shelving and racking systems holding textile bales; workplace clearance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code including manual handling limits, lighting, washroom facilities and emergency response planning.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO) and GST/HST portal at canada.ca
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Alberta business corporation: incorporate under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), obtain the certified articles and minute book, then apply to the CRA through BRO for a federal Business Number and GST/HST registration account. A non-resident entity must provide a Canadian director or a recognized representative resident in Canada, any Canadian office or Alberta jurisdiction address, and the corporate incorporation certificate. CRA issues the BN and GST/HST account within approximately 5 business days; Alberta does not impose a separate provincial sales tax account, and the ATB corporate tax return reporting number is integrated with the CRA BN for federal-provincial administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election is available for Canadian corporations. The Alberta Business Corporation is categorically subject to entity-level federal and provincial income taxation. Available statutory elections include GST/HST group registration under Excise Tax Act s.156 for closely related corporations, GST/HST branch or division registration under s.179, and the election to use the net tax adjustment for financial institutions. Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognized under Canadian domestic law; however, the Income Tax Act includes deductible hybrid mismatch rules (legislative proposals) that restrict deductions where treaty or structural mismatches arise. An Alberta corporation may also elect a fiscal year end and choose the method of capital cost allowance, but no optional pass-through tax classification exists at the federal level.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 annual worldwide taxable supplies threshold for GST/HST small supplier treatment; however, non-resident corporations making taxable supplies in Canada that are not small suppliers must register for GST/HST regardless of whether they have a permanent establishment, and certain foreign entities may be required to register when they solicit orders, advertise, or carry on commercial activity in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or digital furnace control. Tax invoices must contain prescribed information such as vendor identity, BN/GST/HST registration number, date, description, and tax amount. Electronic invoices are accepted, but taxpayers must retain audit evidence. The CRA requires point-of-sale records for retail sales and may inspect accounting systems. No government approval of invoice software is currently required; however, digital bookkeeping and electronic records must be preserved for audit in accessible and legible format.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of finished garments are zero-rated under Schedule VI Part V of the Excise Tax Act. The zero rating applies when tangible personal property is supplied to a non-resident and is exported from Canada, or is delivered outside Canada, as part of the supply. Services, such as brokerage, logistics, or off-price resale services relating to overseas clients, may be zero-rated if provided to a non-resident person and supplied to a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST. The taxpayer must retain documentary evidence that ownership passes outside Canada and that the goods were exported within a reasonable time.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Authorized Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) export declaration (B13A or Canada Export Reporting System confirmation)
Bills of lading / airway bills / freight forwarding evidence
Commercial invoice with terms of sale and FOB export destination
Customs export declarations and tracking proof
Inward remittance certificate or bank transfer confirmation showing foreign-currency payment
Foreign buyer purchase order and non-resident status documentation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits export claims strictly. If zero-rating is ineligible or export documentation is missing, GST/HST becomes payable at 5% with interest from date of supply. The CRA may assess a penalty up to 25% of the tax amount if false statements or careless omissions are made, and may impose gross negligence penalties up to CAD 5,000 or more, plus 50% of tax improperly refunded. Intentional fraud can lead to criminal prosecution, fines, and imprisonment. Retroactive clawbacks are not limited to a four-year reassessment period where misrepresentation is involved; an unlimited reassessment may occur for fraudulent returns.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/CFT enforcement
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains unrestricted currency convertibility under IMF Article VIII; there are no controls on current account transactions, capital account movements, or dividend/royalty/profit remittances for non-resident shareholders. Profit repatriation is subject solely to commercial solvency requirements under the Canada Business Corporations Act and relevant withholding tax obligations (typically 25% unless reduced by treaty, e.g., 5%-15% under the Canada-United States tax treaty). No prior exchange control approval is required for denominating transactions in foreign currency or settling invoices from offshore counterparties. The Canadian dollar (CAD) is freely floating; banks and licensed foreign exchange dealers provide market-rate conversion without central bank intervention.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender requirements in Canada. Exporters may retain proceeds in foreign currency, convert them at market rates, or use them for direct offshore disbursements. Receipts from apparel off-price wholesale liquidation may be held in USD, EUR, or other currencies in offshore or domestic accounts without mandatory repatriation or compulsory conversion. Entities must only ensure proper bookkeeping and tax reporting in CAD for income tax purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium for ancillary treasury functions; Low as a primary bank for capital escrow. Offshore digital EMI platforms (e.g., Wise Business, Stripe Treasury, Payoneer) may be used for commercial cross-border payments and FX conversion, but they are not chartered banks in Canada. To serve Canadian clients, such EMIs must generally register as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC and comply with Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Canadian banks will normally require a domestic operating account as the anchor, with EMIs used solely for settlement efficiency, not custody of bulk liquidity. Legal constraint: an unregistered offshore EMI that accepts Canadian-domiciled funds may itself violate Canadian AML regulations and expose the corporate treasury to compliance risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of a director or authorized signatory is generally required for opening a corporate bank account in Canada, particularly for non-resident-owned entities. A video-conference interview may supplement but does not fully replace the in-person verification step for first-time clients without prior banking history. Remote opening is possible for certain established clients at some Schedule I banks, but under OSFI guidance and bank-specific risk appetite, an in-branch interview at a Canadian branch or a designated international representative office is typical. For an Alberta-domiciled Business Corporation, it is advisable for at least one director or corporate officer to attend an in-person meeting in Calgary or Edmonton with formal identification, corporate seal, and original certified documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of beneficial ownership for non-resident shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate certificate and articles of incorporation; complete share register with names, addresses, and percentages; ultimate beneficial owner disclosure forms (e.g., FINTRAC MSB reporting or bank-specific KYC forms); notarized passport copies and proof of residential address; corporate organizational chart; source of funds declaration for initial capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume wholesale apparel liquidation model flagged as potential invoice fraud or trade-based money laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Finalized supplier agreements with brand authorization or liquidation purchase orders; shipping and logistics documentation (bill of lading, customs entry summary); invoice serial numbers and settlement reconciliation; proof of underlying inventory through warehouse receipts; independent auditor listing of top 100 transactions; detailed margin analysis demonstrating commercial rationality.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained FX conversion or frequent cross-border wire activity to low-cost sourcing jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction rationale memorandum; source and destination ledger with contractual references; counterparty KYC packages for major suppliers and buyers; country-specific sanctions and PEP screening; escalation protocol for transactions exceeding CAD 100,000; audit trail of business emails and purchase orders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Short turnaround time between capital injection and disbursement to third parties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cash-flow forecast model for the liquidation cycle; inventory purchase contracts with delivery milestones; proof of warehouse title and insurance coverage; letter from authorized accounting firm confirming no commingling of personal funds; board resolution approving treasury management policy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections into the Alberta corporate treasury must be routed over SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) for direct wires with full remitter/beneficiary information. The payment purpose should be encoded as 'Foreign Direct Investment – Equity Capital' (CA purpose code reference: 7FCG or equivalent under the Bank of Canada Balance of Payments coding) to distinguish from trade settlement. Verification steps include: (a) confirmation that the sending financial institution is not subject to Canadian sanctions under OFSI/OSFI vetting standards; (b) matching the remitter name with the shareholder registry; (c) adherence to FINTRAC reporting thresholds (CAD 10,000 for electronic funds transfer) using the Electronic Funds Transfer Report (EFTR); (d) settlement in CAD via LVTS/Lynx or a conventional wire transfer by the receiving Canadian bank. No exchange control approval is required. For capital contributions exceeding CAD 250,000, banks may request board-approved source-of-funds evidence and a written confirmation that the injection is genuine equity, not a loan, to avoid inadvertent tax characterization.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for procuring finished garments from offshore vendors may use: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct telegraphic transfers in USD, EUR, or CNY; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) issued via MT700, with full compliance with Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP600); (iii) SWIFT MT202/MT202COV for bank-to-bank cover payments where L/C accumulation is required; (iv) domestic CAD settlement via Interac or ACH when the counterparty has a Canadian clearing presence. Payments to overseas suppliers must be mapped to Bank of Canada trade purpose code 'Goods import / wholesale trade' (e.g., code 10-01 for general merchandise) to avoid AML review. All MT103 messages must include the ISO 20022 transaction reference to match vendor invoices and goods transport data. Use of an international trade desk or trade finance facility may allow netting and issue guaranteed payment corpora where the off-price portfolio has high transaction throughput.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Over-the-Counter (OTC) foreign currency forwards on CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, and CAD/CNY with licensed Canadian Schedule I banks or registered derivatives dealers under the Derivatives Act (Alberta)

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) selectively permitted for exotic or non-convertible currency exposures (e.g., INR, ARS) provided the transaction is booked with an OECD licensed counterparty and does not violate OFSI sanctions policy
Cross-Currency Swaps (CSTS) between CAD and major trade currencies to align asset-liability cash flows on long-term supplier contracts
Plain-vanilla currency options (call/put on USD/CAD) for downside protection on purchase prices
Foreign exchange swap agreements (FX swaps) for short-term rollovers of export proceeds held in USD back into CAD for local working capital

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or extra-provincial registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years may trigger administrative dissolution by the Registrar; late filing may incur revival fees and administrative reinstatement costs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the fiscal year-end; e.g., June 30 for a December 31 year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months; interest compounded daily; repeated failures attract substantially higher penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year-end for annual remittance filers; quarterly or monthly filing if required by CRA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 1% of the balance due plus 1% per month where more than one return is overdue; statutory interest accrues daily.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) Register Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained at the corporation's registered office in Alberta; subject to inspection by law enforcement and the Registrar upon request; no public annual filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation at the incorporation anniversary date; material changes to significant control must be recorded within 15 days of becoming known
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties up to CAD 1,000 for failing to maintain or update the register; potential director liability and court-ordered compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, a mandatory independent audit applies to a distributing corporation (publicly listed or distributing securities), upon shareholder requisition, or by court order. A private non-distributing corporation may dispense with an auditor by unanimous shareholder agreement; no revenue-or-asset-based audit threshold exists for a standard private off-price apparel wholesaler.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for distributing and public corporations; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) commonly applied by private Alberta corporations. CRA accepts either framework when consistently applied.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the ABCA, the ISC Register must be maintained at the registered office or another location in Alberta designated by the board. Annually, at the incorporation anniversary, the corporation must verify that all individuals with significant control (direct or indirect ownership or control of 25% or more of voting shares or de facto control) are correctly recorded. Share transfers must be posted to the Register of Transfers; corresponding ISC changes are logged within 15 days of becoming known. The Alberta Annual Return filing serves as a practical compliance checkpoint, although Alberta does not require public filing of ISC details.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)
Minute Book (minutes of directors' and shareholders' meetings)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined: 15% federal general corporate rate + 8% Alberta general corporate rate. A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) eligible for the small business deduction pays 11% combined (9% federal + 2% Alberta) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income. A non-resident corporation without a permanent establishment (PE) in any province is not entitled to the 10% federal provincial abatement and may face a higher effective federal rate on Canadian-source income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal General Rate Reduction lowers the base federal rate from 28% to 15% on active business income; Alberta imposes a flat 8% general rate and 2% small-business rate; no statutory tax holiday exists for wholesale apparel distributors. Effective tax rate can be reduced by capital cost allowance (accelerated CCA), the small business deduction, the 3-year carryback / 20-year carryforward of non-capital losses, and inventory valuation write-downs to net realizable value for distressed overstock under the inventory rules of the Income Tax Act. No Alberta capital tax or payroll tax applies for corporations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, administered by the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and electronically integrated with the Alberta corporate tax returns under the federal-provincial tax collection agreement. Filing is mandatory through CRA-certified EFILE / XML / web portal software; paper filing is restricted and generally unavailable for corporations with gross revenue exceeding CAD 1,000,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual for each fiscal period. Income tax instalments are payable monthly for most corporations, or quarterly for a CCPC with taxable income below CAD 500,000 and a prior-year tax balance below threshold limits.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The T2 return must be filed no later than six months after the fiscal year-end. The final balance of tax payable is due two months after the fiscal year-end for ordinary corporations, and three months after the fiscal year-end for CCPCs eligible for the small business deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, 9-digit CRA business number, registered office address, fiscal period end date, jurisdiction of incorporation, and Alberta corporate access number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the CRA BN and Alberta extra-provincial registration number; identify the address and nature of the Canadian permanent establishment; confirm whether Canada-Alberta allocation applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue, cost of goods sold, gross profit, operating expenses, and net income before taxes for the fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source revenue attributable to the Canadian PE; intercompany purchase of overstock finished garments from a non-resident affiliate must be recorded at arm's length price and supported by contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income as adjusted for non-capital loss carryovers, capital loss restrictions, and tax accounting adjustments to book income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate taxable income as business income reasonably attributed to the Canadian PE pursuant to section 115 of the Income Tax Act; confirm whether the treaty permanent establishment threshold is exceeded before making the allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 1 - Federal Base Tax and Reductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax computed at 38% of taxable income, less the 10% provincial abatement, the 13% general rate reduction, and the small business deduction where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 10% provincial abatement is available only where the corporation has a PE in a Canadian province; a non-resident without a Canadian PE must revisit the abatement and general rate reduction eligibility before relying on the 23% combined headline rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of Alberta corporate tax at 8% general corporate rate on Alberta-taxable income, with 2% small business rate on the first CAD 500,000 of qualifying active business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Alberta corporate tax applies to income allocated to a PE in Alberta; if no PE exists in Alberta, no provincial allocation is made, but the CRA requires the T2 and related provincial schedules to remain consistent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim for reduced federal and provincial rates on active business income up to the annual business limit of CAD 500,000 for a CCPC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Generally unavailable to non-resident-owned corporations; off-price apparel liquidation trading entities controlled directly or indirectly by non-residents must verify CCPC status and the associated-corporation rules before relying on the reduced rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction of eligible non-capital losses carried forward from prior taxation years and carrybacks applied against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation may deduct Canadian non-capital losses only against income sourced in Canada; the 3-year carryback and 20-year carryforward limits apply; supporting loss continuity schedules must be retained.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing penalty is 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; a repeat offender or a filer criminally convicted for late filing faces an increased penalty of 10% of the unpaid balance plus 2% per month up to 20 months. Daily compounded prescribed-rate interest applies to unpaid tax, late instalments, and penalties. Failure to file information returns such as T5, T106, or NR4 attracts per-day penalties from CAD 25 to CAD 100 per slip up to statutory maximums; gross negligence is penalized at 50% of the understated tax under section 163(2); criminal prosecution under sections 238 and 239 of the Income Tax Act may add fines and imprisonment.
